item.description: The phrase “biblical masculinity” is gaining traction in churches, men’s groups and online forums. item.title: Morning news brief
item.description: How President Trump's influence might affect upcoming Republican primaries, WHO declares ebola outbreak in Africa a global health emergency, jury deliberations begin in OpenAI case.

item.title: Driver of crashed train tested positive for drugs, Thai police say
item.description: The freight train collided with a bus in Bangkok, killing eight people and injuring dozens of others.

item.title: WHO declares Ebola outbreak in DR Congo an international emergency
item.description: The agency added that the outbreak, with around 246 cases and 80 deaths, does not meet the criteria of pandemic emergency.

item.title: Peru's electoral board confirms June 7 presidential runoff
item.description: Authorities confirmed on Sunday the official results of the first round of the presidential elections in early April, with Keiko Fujimori and Roberto Sánchez advancing to the runoff on June 7.

item.title: Drone strikes UAE nuclear plant highlighting risk of renewed war
item.description: A drone strike sparked a fire on the edge of the United Arab Emirates' sole nuclear power plant on Sunday in what authorities called an "unprovoked terrorist attack."

item.title: UK companies linked to payments for small-boat crossings, BBC finds
item.description: Smugglers are directing migrants to pay using a network of British businesses, secret filming reveals.

item.title: Moment two fighter jets collide mid-air at US air show
item.description: Four crew members safely ejected from US Navy jets and are in a stable condition after the collision.

item.title: Executions nearly doubled in the U.S. last year, and soared abroad
item.description: The number of people killed in state-sanctioned executions worldwide rose to a 44-year high in 2025, according to a new report from Amnesty International.

item.title: Are baby boomers like me the luckiest generation in history?
item.description: As young graduates criticise the terms of their student debt, Evan Davis asks whether baby boomers really were the luckiest generation
